plan.notes: Transcribed 2026-11-11 from the official Southern Utah University 2026-2027 General Catalog (current edition, catoid=28) Civil Engineering program page and its linked official degree map workbook, 'Civil Engineering Degree Maps (2026-2027)', 'Civil Engineering (Campus)' tab; the workbook header reads 'Updated for Fall 2026' and prints no per-tab updated date. Semester placement is the university's official sample 4-year campus academic plan (SUU Program Maps, 2026-2027), which the source itself labels a guide only; students confirm specifics in Degree Works with a Student Success Advisor. BS-only program: the catalog page offers no BA option and prints no foreign-language requirement. Every term's courses sum to the map's printed term total (15/15/14/15/14/15/16/16) and the plan to the catalog's printed Total Credits, BS Degree: 120. The catalog's printed blocks reconcile: Core Requirements 83-84 credits (the 29 fixed core courses sum to 77, plus the 3-credit Math or Natural Science Elective and the 3-4 credit Statistics Requirement) plus Civil Engineering Electives 6 credits equals the printed Civil Engineering Curriculum heading of 89-90 credits. The map exercises the 3-credit statistics option, MATH 1031; the catalog's Statistics Requirement also lists MATH 1040 (4 credits), MATH 1190 (3 credits; the option the catalog says Civil Engineering majors are encouraged to take) and MATH 3700 (4 credits). DISCLOSED map/catalog difference, recorded on the catalog side: the map prints 'MATH 1031 Statistical Inference*' where the catalog lists MATH 1031 - Statistical Reasoning (the catalog's 'Statistical Inference' title belongs to MATH 1040); MATH 1031 is recorded under its catalog title. Catalog titles are also recorded where the map shortens them (e.g. CE 2160 'Materials Science for Civil/Construction Engrs*' on the map). The map's two 3-credit Major Elective slots carry the catalog's Civil Engineering Electives list as disclosed on each slot; the catalog list also includes variable-credit CE 4890 (1-3) and ENGR 4900 (1-3) and the 4-credit GEOG 2800, which a 3-credit map slot cannot represent. The catalog's General Education block prints only Core Course Requirements (12+ credits) and Breadth Area Requirements (16+ credits) with 'See General Education for course options'; the map's GE rows are recorded as printed. The map's free-elective rows total 9 credits; the catalog's Free Electives section prints no fixed figure (the total is determined by the General Education courses taken, degree type, additional credits earned and prerequisite courses needed). Program information printed in the catalog: students must earn a minimum overall 2.5 GPA in Civil Engineering major courses to graduate (with a one-semester probationary period once 20 major credits are completed) and must attempt the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination; the program typically leads to licensure/certification in Utah.

The catalog does not itself name MATH 1220; the recommendation is the map's.
